subject.title: [Feature]: Non-interactive command to use Codex OAuth for model provider

question: Should OpenClaw add a non-interactive OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex OAuth setup path, and which callback or token handoff is acceptable for secret-bearing auth material?
rationale: This would create a public auth-provider setup contract around OAuth authorization material, environment/config behavior, and provider routing; automation cannot safely choose that security posture.

options.title: Design safer provider-owned handoff
options.body: Add a provider-owned non-interactive flow that validates PKCE/state, minimizes callback URL exposure, redacts diagnostics, and documents the supported contract before implementation.

options.title: Accept callback URL env import
options.body: Support a callback URL environment import only with explicit state validation, redaction, docs, and upgrade/security proof for shell and CI contexts.

options.title: Defer to existing flows
options.body: Keep API-key, browser/manual paste, and device-code as the supported setup surfaces until upstream Codex exposes a safer stable contract.

recommendation.title: Design safer provider-owned handoff
recommendation.body: Add a provider-owned non-interactive flow that validates PKCE/state, minimizes callback URL exposure, redacts diagnostics, and documents the supported contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The non-interactive provider setup gate and provider-auth plugin migration history point to this account as the best available owner for the auth-surface decision.
